title: Admission gating and fairness stabilization for hosted GPU pools after capacity exhaustions
creator: Priya Kumar
description:
Summary: During the 2025-02-04 hosted API capacity event we observed a multi-minute queue buildup on several GPU pools followed by aggressive throttling that caused elevated error rates and increased 95th/99th token latency for customers on medium and high throughput tiers. This ticket bundles the follow-up engineering work for (A) a deterministic admission-gating layer to prevent unbounded queue amplification, (B) a fairness rebalancer so high-priority traffic cannot permanently starve medium-priority workloads during overload, and (C) a short-term and long-term scaling hardening plan that avoids the brittle oscillation seen in the incident.

Scope and goals: 1) Prevent multi-minute queue amplification from a single noisy workload by adding fast-path admission checks and bounded queue caps per-customer and per-route. 2) Implement a lightweight priority-rebalancer that enforces minimum service share for lower-priority classes (best-effort -> medium -> priority) during sustained overloads. 3) Prevent oscillatory autoscaling behavior by decoupling admission smoothing timescales from autoscaler signals and adding hysteresis. 4) Provide dashboarding and alerting changes so operators can detect runaway queue amplification earlier.

Constraints and trade-offs discussed: - Strict per-customer hard caps reduce tail latency risk but will increase immediate client-visible 429s; we prefer predictable failures to uncontrolled backlog. - Fairness rebalancer introduces extra CPU/coordination overhead; we target a ~1-2% CPU increase on control plane with optimized sampling. - Autoscaler hysteresis will slow down reactive scale-up for short bursts; to compensate we propose a short-lived preemption token to allow emergency short bursts when latency is already degrading.

Operational acceptance criteria: - No pool should present >120s median queue growth for any customer within steady-state traffic. - During synthetic overload tests with mixed priorities, medium-priority throughput should not fall below 30% of steady-state throughput for >60s. - New alerts fire when per-pool queue growth rate exceeds 1 req/sec for 30s and when admission-rate hit ratio > 5%.

comments: 2025-02-11 Priya Kumar: Ticket created after the postmortem sync. Initial plan approved by ENG leads; prioritizing hard caps + fairness rebalancer over immediate aggressive autoscaler tuning.

2025-02-14 Devon Alvarez: POC admission token bucket implemented in runtime branch feat/admission-token. Observed ~45% reduction in queue amplification in local fuzz tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182

2025-02-18 Maya Lopez: Autoscaler hysteresis design posted in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HOSTED/Autoscaler+Hysteresis+Design. Key decision: 60s up-window, 120s down-window with removal of immediate scale-down on single-pool spikes.
2025-02-20 Hana Park: Dashboard panels drafted: per-pool queue growth, admission hits, and per-customer rejected rate. Preview: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted/queue-amplification

2025-02-24 Arun Singh: Priority rebalancer alpha merged to canary. Need performance baseline and swap-in mechanism for rollout without restart. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/269
2025-02-27 Leo Martin: Synthetic mixed-priority harness completed. Nightly runs show rebalancer maintains >35% medium throughput at 2x load; still tuning weight floors.

2025-03-01 Devon Alvarez: Scaled canary to 10% of traffic in us-west-2; observed fewer long-tail spikes during sustained noisy-job runs. Collecting telemetry for a week before broader rollout. Marking in-progress tasks with updated ETA.
